Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

sensitive adjective

easily hurt or upset

also touchy, thin-skinned, oversensitive, sensitive to, sensitive skin, sensitivity

classical

Cic. Att. 1.17.2: quam mollis animus et ad accipiendam et ad dēpōnendam offēnsiōnem
M-O s.v. sensitive

mollis, molle

adjective, third declension; ad + gerundive for what one is sensitive to

soft; of the mind, sensitive, easily moved

Cicero’s word for his brother Quintus, quick to take offence and quick to drop it. Its first sense is soft to the touch (see soft); of character it can also be weak or effeminate, so the context must show the kindly sense.

Other words

  • irrītābilis (inrītābilis), irrītābile — touchy, easily roused

    also used · classical · Cic. Att. 1.17.4 (Lewis & Short); Hor. Ep. 2.2.102: genus vātum, the touchy tribe of poets (Lewis & Short)

  • tener, tenera, tenerum — tender, delicate (of skin, a young plant, a child)

    declension · also used · classical · Lewis & Short, s.v. tener

    Sensitive in body: tenera cutis, sensitive skin.

  • impatiēns + gen. — sensitive to, unable to bear

    adjective, third declension, one ending; with the genitive · also used · classical · Tac. Hist. 2.99: mīles impatiēns sōlis, pulveris, tempestātum (Lewis & Short)

    Post-Augustan (Lewis & Short): sensitive to the sun, to cold. For the cold, Varro and Pliny have alsiōsus (M-O s.v. cold-sensitive).

Examples

  • nam quanta sit in Quīntō frātre meō cōmitās, quanta jūcunditās, quam mollis animus et ad accipiendam et ad dēpōnendam offēnsiōnem, nihil attinet mē ad tē, quī ea nōstī, scrībere

    how kind my brother Quintus is, how pleasant, how sensitive, quick to take offence and quick to let it go, there is no need for me to tell you, who know itCic. Att. 1.17.2

  • inrītābilīs animōs esse optimōrum saepe hominum et eōsdem plācābilīs

    that the best people are often touchy, and just as easily calmedCic. Att. 1.17.4

See also soft, hurt.

SourcesLewis & Short: mollis · Lewis & Short: irritabilis · Lewis & Short: tener · Lewis & Short: impatiens
